Text: What is happening… Where am I???
Cryopod is malfunctioning. Please exit.
Please exit.
Ugh… My head…
Dew beads along the seal, blurring anything beyond.
I need to find a way out.
A recessed hatch sits to your left. You could brute-force it, too.
Cold, stale air. Other pods blink; some open, most sealed.
The bay… looks like most are still asleep.
I should try to find someone.
Status lights stutter. Fallen panels form islands; wires snag your boots.
What happened here? We were supposed to wake at Terminus.
A med-tray has wedged under a panel. Inside: a cracked medkit.
This might save me.
Oh my god!
He is dead…
…looks like he died in cryostasis. Guess he wasn’t so lucky.
A live bundle bars the exit. The frame is hot where arcs bite paint.
If I don’t protect myself, I’ll fry.
Shapes resolve into survivors—faces set, breath visible in the cold.
Good to see someone else awake. There aren’t many of us left.
You recognize Irene from mechanical. The man’s unfamiliar.
What happened?
Irene hesitates. The man answers first.
We were attacked.
By who?
Pirates.
The ship trembles; dust rains from the ceiling.
Escape pods are across the ship. We have to pass an airlock in the maintenance corridor.
We need at least three to clear the way. Can you help us?
The corridor stretches ahead, half-lit and littered with fallen panels. Gravity feels… uneven.
We can’t stay near the cryobay. If the hull gives, that’s it.
Cockpit’s our best bet. From there we route power and unlock the escape pods.
Do we even have a clear path?
Maintenance corridor runs behind the main decks. There’s an access point near the airlock hub.
If it’s not spaced or on fire, that is.
So… fight the pirates or run?
Survive first. Argue about heroics later.
Right. Let’s go.
The others vanish into the fog. For a moment, the hallway feels bigger than the whole ship.
…I should still head for the maintenance corridor. Cockpit, airlocks, escape pods—it’s all through there.
If I stay here, I’m just waiting to die.
The corridor bends like a cracked spine. Frost clings to seams; a big stencil points toward the AIRLOCK HUB.
There. Airlock hub. From there we cut across to the cockpit.
Irene taps the control panel. It spits a dim error glyph.
It’s… not responding. Door’s locked hard.
Let me try.
Darius swipes an access card. The panel chirps—then dies completely.
That didn’t sound like ‘access granted’.
Panel’s dead. No power on this segment.
Great. That means the generator bus to this section is offline.
Can we fix it?
There’s a backup generator room just aft of here. If we bring it online, this door—and the escape pods—should get power.
Or the pirates get power too. But we don’t have a choice.
Lead the way.
The corridor bends like a cracked spine. The AIRLOCK stencil stops at a bulkhead door, its panel dark.
It’s locked… and the panel’s dead.
I don’t have an access card, and even if I did—no power.
A wall locker hangs half-open. Above it, a ventilation grate sits askew. Air whistles softly through the gap.
Maybe I can’t open the door…
…but I might be able to go around it.
Light spills through an open ventilation shaft. Cold air brushes your face, carrying oil and ozone.
If this runs above the corridor, it might drop me near the cockpit.
Or into a spinning fan. Or a vacuum leak. Great options all around.
The ship shudders again. Dust drifts from the ceiling.
Yeah. I’m not staying out here.
The shaft narrows around you. Ahead, a large fan spins so fast the blades blur. Each gust shoves stale air into your face.
Yeah, definitely the ‘spinning fan’ option.
A maintenance terminal blinks weakly beside the shaft, half-buried in cables.
If I can hack that terminal, maybe I can slow the fan or kill the power.
If I miscalculate… I become ventilation confetti.
The door hisses open into a cramped generator room. A backup reactor squats in the center like a sleeping heart. Its status ring is dark.
Here we are. Backup generator for this section.
Looks like it got knocked offline when the pirates hit us.
Can we bring it back without blowing ourselves up?
We reroute the damaged lines, reset the breakers, and spin it up slowly. Simple… in theory.
Panel’s still got some life.
The console flickers on, showing a messy diagram of power nodes and warning triangles.
I’ll guide you, Ryan. You’ve got steady hands from cryo calibration, right?
I woke up ten minutes ago from a malfunctioning pod.
Then you’re used to things going wrong. Perfect.
The generator’s status ring spins up from red to steady green. Lights flicker back to life in the corridor.
We did it. Power’s routing—airlock hub should be online.
Move! Before someone shoots it off again.
You sprint back. The once-dead door hisses open, revealing a cross-corridor and a row of escape pods. Some are warped and blackened. A few remain intact, lights pulsing calmly.
There are still pods left…
Three seats. That’s exactly how many we need.
For now.
Another tremor hits. Somewhere deeper in the ship, something tears. The lights dim, then steady.
We launch, we send a distress beacon. Someone will pick us up before we suffocate. Probably.
Better odds than staying here.
I’ll prime the pod. Ryan, grab emergency supplies; Irene, sync the beacon to our coordinates.
You toss a medkit and a flickering datapad into the pod. Irene’s fingers dance over the controls, locking in a broadcast loop.
Beacon’s ready. Last call: anyone want to stay on the exploding ship?
…Pass.
Door’s closing. Strap in.
The pod hatch seals. Through the small viewport, you see the ship’s wounded hull receding. Stars stretch into the void as thrusters ignite.
We made it. Somehow.
One disaster at a time. When we’re picked up, we tell them what happened here.
And maybe next time, we get a quiet transport job.
Outside, the broken ship drifts silently, its beacon pulsing into the dark. Your pod carries you toward the unknown—but away from certain death.
The generator shudders as you reroute the last line. For a heartbeat, its status ring flashes green—then flares red.
Wait—no, that’s too much load—
A sharp bang echoes through the room. The lights go out. The console dies, mid-error.
Tell me that was a fuse.
…That was not a fuse.
Can we try again?
The core’s fried. We just killed the last clean supply to this section.
The distant alarms wind down, one by one, strangled as power bleeds away. The ship groans, then falls eerily quiet.
So no power to the airlocks. No pods. No doors.
No radio. No long-range beacon from here, either.
…We’re stuck.
In the dim emergency strips, their faces look hollow. The floor vibrates faintly as something detonates far away, then nothing.
Maybe the primary systems can still auto-broadcast a distress signal. Someone could find the wreck.
In a few weeks. Or years.
We have air and water for… how long?
Long enough to be uncomfortable. Not long enough to be old.
The three of you sit in the failing light of the dead generator room while the ship drifts into the dark, silent and powerless.
I should have stayed in cryo.
At least now you know why they invented dreamless sleep.
The fan whines down, blades slowing until they stop with a final clunk. The duct ahead opens into a grille above the cockpit door.
Didn’t get turned into confetti. I’ll take that as a win.
You squeeze through and drop to the deck, landing in front of the cockpit. Its door stands ajar. Smoke curls lazily from a damaged console.
Inside, the bridge is a mess of dead screens and cracked panels. The forward window is spidered but intact, framing a field of distant stars.
Okay, ship. Show me something good.
One main console still glows. A status display shows partial power, life support holding, hull breached in several sections. No other crew signatures detected.
…Guess it’s just me.
A menu flashes: AUTOPILOT, DISTRESS BEACON, ESCAPE POD CONTROL.
All right. Step one: tell the universe I’m not dead yet.
You route what’s left of the power into the beacon. A green indicator blinks: BROADCAST ACTIVE.
Step two… see if any pods survived.
A schematic of the ship appears. Most escape pods are crossed out, but one cluster near the bow still shows green.
Perfect. One last ride.
You set the ship to orient itself to minimize further hull damage. The engines cough weakly, nudging the vessel into a slow, controlled spin.
If anyone finds this wreck, maybe they’ll want to know what happened.
You trigger a final log, speaking into the recorder.
This is Ryan from the Terminus run. We were attacked by pirates. Most of us never woke up. If you’re hearing this… I made it to the pods.
You cut the log, lock in the beacon, and head for the last working escape pod.
No heroes. Just a survivor.
As the pod launches, the bridge recedes behind you—a lone, wounded ship broadcasting its story into the void, while you arc away toward an uncertain, but living, future.
You squint at the spinning blades, judge the timing, and take a breath.
I can make that.
You can’t.
There’s a single, blinding moment of motion and metal. Then nothing at all.
The fan keeps spinning, indifferent, pushing air through an empty shaft in a ship that drifts farther into the dark.
